assessment: Full assembly gives workers an opportunity to encounter insertion problems and check an order before dispatch, but its benefit is unmeasured. The 11-minute median exceeds the time target; seven of ten customers achieved their arrangement unaided. Five partition complaints suggest a contents problem without establishing a verified defect rate. Mixed batches contain every extreme delay, while repeated three-compartment orders take seven to nine minutes: this limiting observation suggests the incumbent sometimes approaches the target, but layout complexity and switching are confounded. Overlapping partition widths also limit a width-only explanation of reinsertion. Neither sequence effects nor fit causes are established.

openings.claim: Switching between order configurations may contribute to selection and checking delays beyond the work required by compartment count.
openings.delta: Separates a potentially changeable sequencing cost from inherent assembly complexity.
openings.prediction: For identical layout and color workloads, blocked sequences reduce selection/checking time relative to alternating sequences, even within the same compartment count.
openings.probe: Use reusable sample orders with both workers and identical contents in blocked and alternating sequences, counterbalancing sequence order. Record selection, insertion, checking and packing separately, plus contents errors. Keep accepted orders and dispatch timing unchanged; limit rehearsal to available working time.
assumptions: Rehearsal time is available before the fixed deadline.
Samples can be reused without material wear dominating results.

openings.claim: Does uncertainty about short-partition placement persist when contents and insertion feasibility are verified, and does an order-specific diagram reduce it?
openings.delta: Distinguishes information ambiguity from missing, incorrect or mechanically unusable parts.
openings.prediction: If diagram ambiguity contributes, customers receiving an order-specific diagram ask fewer placement questions and more often finish unaided despite equivalent verified parts.
openings.probe: Assign five of the ten willing participants to the current diagram and five to a hand-drawn order-specific diagram, using matched layouts and verified reusable samples. Record unaided completion within ten minutes, placement questions and insertion failures. Treat results as exploratory; price production diagrams before adoption against both cost limits.
assumptions: Sample verification does not itself reveal placement to participants.
Any production change must also fit workshop time and cost limits.
